title: Multi-region SaaS with a service mesh and AI agent

organisation.name: Vantora
organisation.size: 1,100 staff; 3,000 business customers in two regions
organisation.summary: Vantora collects and unifies customer events for 3,000 businesses. Customer apps and SDKs call an API edge with a WAF that routes REST traffic to the profile service and GraphQL to a gateway; services run on Kubernetes behind a service mesh with mTLS. The export service writes data into customers' own cloud accounts by assuming a cross-account role through workload identity, and data is encrypted with customer-managed keys. An AI agent answers questions about a tenant's data with profile and export tools. A GitOps pipeline deploys signed images, and a third-party feature-flag service switches features in production.

container_kubernetes.summary: Any pod in the export namespace can assume the export role through workload identity
Admission checks a signature, not which pipeline built the image

devsecops_supply_chain.summary: An image signed by a test pipeline is admitted to production
Feature flags change production behaviour outside the delivery pipeline

cloud_security.summary: The export role can write into any customer's account, chosen by a request field
Revoking a customer-managed key does not stop access for a day

api_security.summary: GraphQL aliases batch reads across tenants where one resolver skips the tenant check
The export mutation takes a tenant id from the request body

application_security.summary: A feature flag turns on a debug endpoint that echoes internal headers and tokens
Export destinations accept a URL, so the export service fetches internal addresses

zero_trust.summary: Mesh policy trusts every workload in the namespace to call the export service
A flag-console account without SSO can change what the agent is allowed to do

ai_llm_security.summary: A flag rule enables the agent's export tool for every tenant
A profile field written by an end user carries instructions the agent follows

data_security.summary: Exports land in another customer's account
Profile data goes to the LLM provider inside tool results

identity_access.summary: Tenant API keys reach other tenants' data where a resolver trusts the tenant argument
Two contractor accounts on the flag console have no SSO or MFA

incident_response.summary: A customer reports export files in its account that belong to someone else
Agent traces show export tool calls for tenants the users do not belong to

network_security.summary: Services can reach any internet address, so tool output can be sent outside
The edge routes REST straight to the profile service, skipping GraphQL's limits

reviewNotes: Advanced: three subtle trusts (namespace-scoped role trust, namespace-wide mesh authorisation, flags enabling agent tools outside the pipeline). Present controls with limits: admission (signed by whom?), CMK (cached keys), WAF (no GraphQL bodies), cost limits (aliases).
